name: Cultural liberalism
summary: Cultural liberalism is the social side of liberalism: individuals, not custom, religion or the state, decide how they live, so long as they do not harm others. It favours personal freedom in sexuality, family, religion and expression, equal treatment and secular public institutions, and it is silent on or divided about economic policy.
scope: The mainstream cultural, civil or social-liberal strand descending from Mill's On Liberty and Enlightenment toleration, as described in the Wikipedia article and the Stanford Encyclopedia's account of liberalism, including its Western postwar moral liberalization. Economic positions are treated as undetermined; the more radical civil-libertarian variant is noted but not used as the baseline.

keyFigures.name: Henry David Thoreau

sources.title: On Liberty
sources.author: John Stuart Mill
sources.usedFor: Harm principle, liberty of discussion, individuality and eccentricity, limits of social authority over self-regarding conduct.

sources.title: Liberalism
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Toleration, freedom of conscience, equal basic liberty, pluralism, neutrality and the private sphere.

sources.title: Cultural liberalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, social positions such as abortion and same-sex marriage, secularization roots, and the point that adherents differ on fiscal policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is an economic question on which people holding socially liberal views are explicitly described as divided.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology concerns cultural norms, not economic organization; adherents range from market liberals to social democrats.

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership of utilities is outside the cultural-liberal core, and adherents split along ordinary economic lines.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels are a fiscal matter on which self-described cultural liberals disagree.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporate regulation is an economic question left open; Mill himself accepted some regulation but the cultural strand does not prescribe it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare levels are fiscal policy on which cultural liberals are explicitly divided.

worker-ownership.rationale: Business ownership structures are not part of the cultural-liberal programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Liberal presumption favours freedom and a private sphere that need not be justified to the state, so mass surveillance for security is generally resisted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Mill rejects restricting sale of alcohol or opium to protect buyers from themselves, and civil libertarian cultural liberals extend this to drugs, though many accept some regulation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Mill's liberty of discussion opposes silencing opinions, but modern cultural liberals are split on hate-speech laws, so the lean is mild.

strong-leader.rationale: Mill warns against concentrated power and the tyranny of majorities, and cultural liberals favour constraints on executives.

state-harmful.rationale: Cultural liberals want a limited sphere for the state over private life, but not abolition of it; Mill still assigns it protective functions.

decide-locally.rationale: The ideology says little on decentralization; its concern is individual rather than territorial autonomy.

traditional-family.rationale: Cultural liberalism holds individuals may choose whether to follow norms, so it rejects the family model as an obligatory foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Wikipedia cites same-sex marriage as a standard cultural-liberal position expressing equal treatment and individual self-determination.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion rights are named alongside same-sex marriage as the typical socially liberal stance on personal choice.

more-religion-public.rationale: The ideology arose by challenging religious conformity and favours secularism in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equal treatment and expansion of civil rights are central, though remedies like preferences are debated.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mill treats custom as often mistaken for nature and values diversity over conformity, so preserving tradition as such is not a goal.

free-trade.rationale: Mill favoured free trade but the cultural strand is not an economic doctrine and adherents differ.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The ideology does not address foreign policy and adherents are divided.

open-borders.rationale: Pluralism inclines toward openness but the doctrine does not address borders, and adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: Mill warns that concentrating functions in the state makes citizens dependent and stifles liberty; economic planning itself is not core.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic ownership forms are left open by this socially focused ideology.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax-structure question outside the cultural-liberal core.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare design is a fiscal matter on which cultural liberals differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is outside the doctrine; adherents are split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mill's defence of free discussion and objection to silencing opinion are incompatible with a single ideological party leading the state.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberalism is associated with democratic rights, though Mill also warns that majorities can tyrannize, so the answer is moderate.

direct-votes.rationale: Mill's fear of majority tyranny cuts against plebiscites on rights, but the doctrine does not address referendums.

natural-rulers.rationale: Liberalism's equal basic liberty and equal treatment reject innate fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Liberals generally prefer peaceful means but the doctrine is not pacifist; adherents vary.

separate-church-state.rationale: Cultural liberalism developed from challenging religious conformity and the Reformation's individual conscience, favouring secular public institutions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mill criticizes laws grounded in religious rules such as Sabbath laws and pork bans as impositions on those who do not share the belief.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equal treatment and pluralism are incompatible with defining the nation by one ethnic group.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberals prize equal liberty and treatment; equality of outcomes is debated and not core to the cultural strand.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mill values self-development but also stresses harm to others; the doctrine does not call self-interest morally good as such.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cultural liberalism puts individual self-determination first; Mill's harm principle limits only conduct harming others.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mill condemns mistaking custom for nature and champions challenging stagnant custom, the opposite of restoration.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution is an economic question left open.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial rule over a class conflicts with Mill's protection of liberty against social and political tyranny.

taxation-theft.rationale: Mill accepted a state with protective functions funded by taxation; the cultural strand does not hold this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill states that society may limit liberty only to prevent harm to others, and cultural liberalism cites this as its foundation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberalism puts the individual at the centre, though multicultural liberals sometimes accept group accommodations.

conscription.rationale: Compulsory service overrides self-determination; Mill allowed exceptions for defence, so mild.

exit-over-voice.rationale: SEP mentions exit rights in toleration debates but the doctrine does not rank exit above voting.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social liberals often accept this while civil libertarians stress non-interference; the cultural core is split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equal moral worth and equal treatment are central, and cultural liberals reject racial hierarchy.

total-state.rationale: Mill's whole argument is that the state and society must leave a large sphere of individual liberty, including in culture and education.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberals differ between universalists and value pluralists such as Berlin.

single-common-good.rationale: Reasonable pluralism about how to live is a liberal premise, so one common good worked out by reason is resisted.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A national homeland claim is a question of nationalism that the doctrine does not address, and cultural liberals hold varied views.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights for diasporas are a nationality-policy question outside the cultural-liberal core, with adherents split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance is an economic question, and the sources say adherents differ on economic matters.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is not part of the doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: Liberals often link them but cultural liberals are divided.

national-self-determination.rationale: The doctrine centres on individuals rather than nations, so it has no settled answer on national statehood.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of force abroad is foreign policy, which cultural liberalism does not cover, and adherents differ.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mill's defence of free inquiry favours reason, but many cultural liberals respect religious conscience, so mild.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare design is a fiscal question where adherents differ.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale says neither economic approach is prescribed; silence is not a position, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Relations between employers and workers are economic, and cultural liberalism does not prescribe either cooperation or conflict.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale says neither economic approach is prescribed; silence is not a position, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

workers-nation.rationale: How the working class should organize is a socialist-theory question to which cultural liberalism gives no answer.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equal treatment and freedom to ignore cultural norms oppose legally fixed roles for men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: Mill criticizes laws based on religious rules and restricting self-regarding transactions.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal treatment before the law is central to liberalism's equal basic liberty.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: SEP records liberal toleration of religious and cultural minorities; forced assimilation conflicts with freedom to choose cultural norms.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in liberal pluralist thinking; cultural liberals reject it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Cultural liberals typically accept structural disadvantage claims but it is not a defining doctrine.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mill allowed state education and some regulation; cultural liberals split between minimal and social-liberal states.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: SEP stresses equal basic liberty, and cultural liberalism centres equal treatment.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal treatment under law favours common civil law, although liberals also accept some religious accommodation.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of conscience and religion is a core liberal commitment.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Mill rejects imposing religion-based dietary rules on others, such as pork bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Secularism and the individual-conscience heritage favour non-confessional state schooling.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Liberal legitimacy is generally tied to consent, though the cultural strand focuses elsewhere.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade targets are economic policy, which the sources describe as divisive among adherents.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Close to the harm principle but a libertarian absolutism cultural liberals do not hold; they accept state coercion to prevent harm.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mill praises diversity of experiments in living, but the strand does not endorse struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Free discussion argues against banning parties, while militant-democracy views also exist among liberals, so split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not a defining cultural-liberal concept; adherents hold varying conceptions of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism favours checks on power, though the cultural strand focuses on individual rights.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party leading the working class contradicts liberal individualism and free discussion.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rawlsian priority is liberal but not a cultural-liberal doctrine; adherents split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is an economic matter left open.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law is not part of the cultural core.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Mill values diversity of character and ways of living as the source of progress, rejecting this claim.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Civil liberties are the core of the ideology and suspension to fight internal enemies is resisted.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of information contradicts Mill's argument for liberty of thought and discussion.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization length is immigration policy the doctrine does not specify, and adherents vary.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside political doctrine.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mill opposes restricting expression to protect others from their own moral or aesthetic harm; cultural liberalism opposes moral censorship.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is foreign policy outside the cultural-liberal remit, with adherents divided.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Forbidding a voluntary arrangement between adults interferes with self-regarding choice.

people-in-arms.rationale: A militia in place of a professional army is a defence-policy question left open by the doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The strand is linked to urbanization and loosened moral norms, and rejects privileging a way of life as morally better.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Liberals split between relativism and a liberal standard; Berlin's pluralism supports it, universalists do not.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Free inquiry favours reasoned contest, but religious teaching in state schools is resisted by secular liberals.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Mill's self-regarding conduct principle opposes legal restriction of adults' consumption.

minority-language-support.rationale: Liberal toleration of minority cultures supports accommodation, although neutrality debates exist.

religious-exemptions.rationale: SEP notes liberal accommodation of religious objectors such as the Amish in Yoder, though not unlimited.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill argues in chapter 3 that conformity to custom stifles development and eccentricity should be encouraged.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt policy is economic and geopolitical, and the sources identify no cultural-liberal position.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are an economic and ethical question on which cultural liberals disagree, with no doctrinal answer.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is defence policy outside cultural liberalism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The mode of selecting a head of state is an institutional choice the doctrine leaves open.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary governance is economic and technical, and the sources say adherents differ on economics.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Left open by the cultural strand.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not part of the cultural-liberal core, and adherents differ.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale turns on church property, privileges or separation, and the statement now asks only whether religious institutions should operate under the government's authority.

reviewHistory.rationale: Secularism favours separation, but curbing clergy and religious property can infringe religious freedom, so liberals split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Whether the head of state should be above party politics is a constitutional-design matter left open.

character-from-environment.rationale: Mill stresses custom's shaping force and individual choice; no settled position.

space-expansion.rationale: Space as a civilizational goal is outside cultural liberalism, which focuses on norms and personal freedom.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical idea of mixing rule by the few and the many is not a cultural-liberal concern.

equal-parenting.rationale: Presumptive equal custody is a family-law detail on which adherents may split between equality and case-by-case judgement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is an internal dispute in Maoist theory unrelated to cultural liberalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Redistribution of agricultural land is an economic question the sources leave open for cultural liberals.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of conscience and religion is core to liberalism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mill opposes coercing self-regarding conduct, which covers dress; he does not discuss dress laws specifically.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Liberal toleration accepts cultural institutions but group autonomy raises individual-rights tensions.

ban-cartels.rationale: Economic regulation is not part of the cultural core.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Mill warns of the tyranny of the majority, so minority protections against majorities are favoured.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equality is valued but mandated parity is debated among liberals.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs are an economic doctrine the cultural-liberal strand does not hold or oppose by definition.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Conditions in trade deals are economic policy on which adherents differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal basic liberty and equal treatment oppose inherited legal privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mill himself allowed it for societies not ready for free discussion, but modern cultural liberals reject it as paternalism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Mill warned against state control over what is taught and for uniformity of opinion.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Liberals split between equal treatment and remedial preferences.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence in former imperial regions is foreign policy outside cultural liberalism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal treatment is central, so private discrimination is opposed, though some civil libertarians would defend it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Protections against majority tyranny fit the demand for a secured individual sphere.

minority-veto.rationale: Mill protects individuals in self-regarding conduct but not a blanket veto over collective decisions.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mill fears majority tyranny, so parliamentary supremacy is not endorsed outright.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The ethics of using animals is outside the cultural-liberal sources and adherents vary.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Individuality allows varied lives, but the doctrine does not rank political withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mill worried about conformity under mass opinion, but the doctrine does not take a Frankfurt School view.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Liberals agree on rejecting fascism but differ on constitutionalizing it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Liberals criticize both, but the doctrine takes no stand on equivalence.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Whether to keep contested monuments is a culture-war issue on which cultural liberals are divided between free expression of heritage and rejecting honours.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Service policy on domestic violence is not defined by the doctrine, and adherents differ on how to weigh gender asymmetries.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberalism claims universal basic liberties, though value pluralists allow variety.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for the armed forces conflicts with liberal constitutionalism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognizing domestic work as paid labour is a gender-economic proposal on which cultural liberals have no settled stance.

bound-labor.rationale: Mill holds that a person may not sell themselves into bondage; he does not discuss serfdom as such.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The doctrine has no position on elite corruption; adherents vary.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority based on personal oaths conflicts with liberal rule by law and equal treatment.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical rebirth from decadence presumes a single national ideal, against Mill's diversity of lives and criticism of conformity.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Cultural liberalism is silent on economic policy and its adherents are described as divided on it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension financing is an economic question on which social liberals are divided.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Adherents back equal treatment, but many liberals favour an intent standard while others accept effects tests, so they are split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Economic questions are left open by the doctrine and adherents differ on how far to curb business influence.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic policy is undetermined for cultural liberals, so a job guarantee is neither required nor excluded.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Liberals split between duties grounded in consent or fairness and the view that unjust laws do not bind; the sources do not settle it.

non-intervention.rationale: Liberals are divided between respecting sovereignty and intervening for rights, and the sources are silent on it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Toleration and equal treatment of minorities are core, and conspiracy theories about a minority contradict them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Cultural liberals defend access to legal marriage, including same-sex marriage, rather than removing the institution, though some favour state neutrality.

informal-organisation.rationale: The doctrine is neutral on organisational form; it protects freedom of association whatever shape groups take.

religious-nation.rationale: Secular public institutions and freedom of conscience are central, so a religiously defined nation is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal questions are not part of the cultural-liberal core and adherents differ on them.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Cultural liberalism is silent on how public services are delivered, and its adherents are described as divided on fiscal and welfare policy.

religion-illusion.rationale: It treats religion as a matter of private conscience and defends its free exercise, rather than dismissing it as an illusion that will fade.

majority-settlement.rationale: Equal treatment, pluralism and freedom of residence make state steering of ethnic settlement contrary to liberal principles.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Liberal toleration treats all persons as equals regardless of heritage, so a historical tie does not outrank the rights of present residents.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The harm principle in On Liberty bars criminalising consensual private conduct between adults, and cultural liberalism supports same-sex equality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mill argues liberty of discussion and association are essential and that society may not suppress dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Mill and the toleration tradition reject penalising opinion or religious practice, including blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Liberalism rests on equal basic liberty and consent of the governed, which is hostile to governing territories for the metropole.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Liberal neutrality and toleration reject removing rulers by force over a failure to apply religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Liberalism values self-government and individuals taking part in decisions, but cultural liberals are mostly content with representative institutions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Cultural liberals stress equal treatment and anti-discrimination, but adherents split on intersectional frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Cultural liberalism's emphasis on individual self-definition and equal treatment supports legal recognition of gender identity; some adherents differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: The harm principle and respect for autonomy over one's own life support assisted dying, and cultural liberals typically back it with safeguards.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Toleration and equal liberty reject treating a whole religion as incompatible with liberal society; mainstream cultural liberals stress pluralism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Liberalism holds authority comes from the consent of the governed and not from God, with public institutions secular.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Cultural liberals value secular public institutions but also freedom of conscience and expression, so adherents divide on dress bans.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic positions are undetermined in cultural liberalism, and adherents differ on fiscal and welfare policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Liberalism opposes hereditary privilege, though the cultural strand rarely addresses succession directly.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Economic positions are undetermined for the cultural strand, so adherents are split on lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Liberalism moved from property qualifications to universal suffrage and cultural liberals support equal civic rights regardless of wealth.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mill defended free expression as valuable in itself; cultural liberals mostly hold that formal freedoms are real despite unequal resources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law and government under public, general legal rules is a core liberal commitment.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equal civic and political rights regardless of race or ethnicity are central to liberalism.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Mill's harm principle and personal freedom mean adults should marry across religions without legal restriction.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Cultural liberalism stresses toleration of religious minorities and rejects singling out groups by faith.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Cultural liberalism favours toleration and individual conscience over inherited authority, so it welcomes believers rethinking doctrine in light of reason.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Economic questions are undetermined in cultural liberalism, and its adherents are divided on wealth and liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The sources name sexual freedom and same-sex marriage as cultural-liberal causes, but not military service specifically.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Cultural liberalism favours state neutrality in religion and individual conscience, so state promotion of atheism in schools violates it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Welfare policy is where socially liberal adherents explicitly differ, so there is no common position.

term-limits.rationale: Institutional design is outside the cultural strand and adherents are split.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Equal treatment regardless of sex is central, though liberal respect for religious freedom of association makes churches' internal rules a split point.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Equality between spouses and individual autonomy in family life are core to cultural liberalism, which rejects customary patriarchal authority.

rent-control.rationale: Economic policy is left open by this strand and adherents differ on market intervention, so nothing is stated on rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is an economic question on which cultural liberals are split; the strand itself is silent.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Mill condemns state moulding of people 'to be exactly like one another' and defends individuality, which is opposed to drilled, state-run youth organisations.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is a security question the strand does not address and adherents are divided.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Distributive and property questions are left open by cultural liberalism; adherents range from market to welfare liberals.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The harm principle permits resisting harm to oneself or others, so most adherents would not call self-defence wrong, though pacifist liberals exist.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Adherents are split: many accept constructionist views of gender while others hold sex to be biological; the strand takes no line.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Liberal neutrality, secular public institutions and pluralism reject framing politics as a struggle between good and evil.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Adherents differ on whether religious traditions should be judged by an external standard; the strand takes no line.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equal treatment regardless of origin is a core liberal commitment, which rules out reserving economic life for a national majority.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Economic questions are left open by the profile, so adherents are split on public ownership of services.

second-chamber.rationale: Constitutional design is not part of cultural liberalism; liberals differ on bicameralism.

family-wage.rationale: Economic matters are left open by the profile, so adherents are split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Liberal privacy values favour it, but the harm principle allows limits against crime; adherents are split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Mill's defence of freedom of expression and of private conduct supports pseudonymous participation, though he does not address the internet.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill's harm principle treats the individual as sovereign over himself, not a means to collective ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Cultural liberalism is secular in public institutions but leaves private spiritual life to the individual; adherents are split.

gm-crops.rationale: Outside the doctrine; adherents are split.

dense-cities.rationale: Outside the doctrine; adherents are split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Cultural liberalism treats people as individuals under equal treatment and rejects group identity by race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Liberals are divided between pacifist and interventionist positions on war; the doctrine does not settle it.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal individual citizenship and secular public institutions point to common electorates rather than separate religious ones.

free-public-college.rationale: Cultural liberalism is silent on or divided about economic policy, so tuition policy is left undetermined.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Economic and environmental policy instruments are not part of its core, and liberals split between price-based and regulatory tools.

women-distinct-values.rationale: It stresses equal treatment and individual rather than group-typical outlooks, so giving weight to women's typical values as such runs against its individualism.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic positions are treated as undetermined for this strand, so capital controls are left open.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Economic and international policy are undetermined in cultural liberalism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Liberalism works through law, rights and constitutional reform and rejects smashing the state.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Economic questions are undetermined in cultural liberalism.

sacred-nation.rationale: Individuals, not custom or the collective, decide how they live, so a sacred nation is not a liberal view.

public-service-media.rationale: Free expression is valued but state funding is an economic question the core leaves open.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Liberal toleration treats religious belief as a matter of conscience and does not assert a single underlying truth.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine is silent on class politics and adherents differ.

ban-fgm.rationale: A harm to a non-consenting person is the case where the harm principle justifies legal prohibition.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal treatment before the law regardless of sex is central to cultural liberalism.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The doctrine is indifferent on how languages are named.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The harm principle supports compensation for harm, but adherents are split on tort versus agency regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Cultural liberalism favours equal citizenship and secular public institutions over customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Individual liberty is central, so adherents resist overriding it, though many back environmental protection.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Adherents split between integration-minded liberals and multiculturalists; the doctrine does not settle it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cultural liberalism is the social side of liberalism and is silent or divided on labour and economic questions.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Liberalism pairs elections with protected individual rights, so cultural liberals would say a government whose policies violate those rights is not fully democratic.

premarital-sex.rationale: Individuals decide how they live provided they harm no one, which covers sexual conduct outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Mill's defence of free expression and its harm principle leave no room for cutting off a population's communications to keep order.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic policy is outside cultural liberalism, and liberals are divided over welfare design.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal treatment and individual rights are core, and Mill himself argued for women's equal political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Cultural liberals are split between a secularist reading that blames religious authority and a tolerant reading that rejects the generalisation.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The liberal tradition holds both property-based and community views of first ownership, and the cultural core does not decide the question.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Cultural liberalism has secularization roots and treats religion as private conscience, so it does not hold scripture to be inerrant as a public truth.

national-church-status.rationale: Liberal neutrality and equal toleration mean no religion should be privileged in law; Mill and the Stanford account both stress this.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Liberalism holds that people may not be punished without due process and equal basic liberty; killing without trial is contrary to its rule-of-law core.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Adherents divide on resources and property; left-libertarians favour this, most social liberals do not.

self-ownership.rationale: Mill's harm principle makes each person sovereign over their own body and mind, though the label and its labour implications are not Mill's wording.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Fiscal policy is explicitly left open; adherents differ on taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is a fiscal question on which adherents differ.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Adherents split between market liberals who oppose privilege and social liberals indifferent to it.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Liberal neutrality and secular public institutions mean politics should not be sorted by religious denomination.

national-resource-control.rationale: Economic questions are left open and adherents differ.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The strand is silent on or divided about economic questions.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Economic policy is undetermined in this strand.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Adherents are split, and the strand's focus is equal treatment, not an empirical claim about racism.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Mill is silent on natural law, and liberals are split between legal positivism and civil disobedience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Economic policy is undetermined in this strand.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The strand has no class politics, and attitudes to patriotism vary.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Welfare levels are fiscal policy on which cultural liberals are explicitly divided. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Laws should not impose religious or customary rules of conduct on people who do not share them.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill criticizes Sabbath laws and religious dietary bans as impositions on non-believers, and cultural liberalism rests on freedom from norm conformity.

missingStatements.text: Adults should be free to end a marriage without having to prove fault.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill suggests marriage and similar engagements should be dissoluble more easily than they were.

notes: Economic questions are answered 0 with medium confidence because the sources say adherents differ on fiscal policy; this reflects genuine indifference of the doctrine, not avoidance. Civil-libertarian adherents would answer more strongly on drugs, speech, guns and surveillance.
